tier: Free trial (500 MB on request), dynamic residential per GB and static ISP

free_tier.stated: One-off 500 MB free trial of overseas native IPs, claimed after e-mail registration by contacting customer service (support chat or Telegram); not self-serve, no standing free tier.
free_tier.notes: Metering is the traffic of the trial allowance; the vendor does not say which direction counts (unverified). The smallest paid purchase is the 2-50 GB dynamic tier at 1.10 USD per GB, 2.20 USD total.

per_object_cap.stated: not applicable: a traffic plan or an address, not an object

retention.stated: 'Traffic never expires' on the dynamic residential plan and 'unused IPs never expire' on the short-term residential IP plan. The static ISP product bills by validity period: 7 days, 30 days or 90 days.
retention.notes: Static ISP 'Billing starts after IP extraction'.

egress.terms: Dynamic residential is billed per GB ('Billed by GB usage'); static ISP is 'Unlimited traffic'; the unlimited products are priced per day, by bandwidth (38.33 USD per day) or by port (0.3 USD per day per port).

interface_detail: HTTP(S) and SOCKS5 forward proxy in username-password and API modes; sticky sessions of 1 to 120 minutes or rotating; a web dashboard at dashboard.novproxy.com.
tooling: Any client that speaks an HTTP or SOCKS5 proxy with credentials, or the vendor's API mode.
chaining: The vendor's gateway is an HTTP or SOCKS5 forward proxy, so it is dialled from a host that can open outbound proxy connections (a rented or free virtual machine); the upstream then sees an address from the vendor's pool instead of the host's own.

limits.value: dynamic residential per GB: 1.10 USD per GB at 2-50 GB, 0.90 at 51-200 GB, 0.70 at 201-999 GB, 0.47 at the TB plan (470.00 USD total)
sticky session length 1 to 120 minutes; the port-based unlimited product rotates each IP for up to 30 minutes

limits_note: Static ISP is priced per IP by country and kind, for example United States native 4.0 USD, Germany broadcast 3.2 USD, Japan native 5.5 USD, Korea native 6.0 USD, for 7, 30 or 90 days, with 5% to 25% volume discounts from 6 to 800+ IPs. The home page headlines 'Long-term static ISP Just 3.2 USD per month'.
binding_note: The purchased GB is the quantity that runs out; the 0.47 USD per GB floor needs the TB plan, and the small tiers cost 1.10 USD per GB.

identity_cost.detail: Registration is by e-mail address and a password of 8 to 22 characters with letters and numbers, plus a slider captcha. The vendor states 'without submitting complicated qualifications'; no ID document or card is asked before the trial. Payment methods for paid plans are unverified.

reliability_note: The vendor states 99.9% success and under 0.5 s response on the home page, unverified here. A static ISP product is sold in two kinds named 'Native' and 'Broadcast'; the pages do not say what the registration class of either kind is. The trial is claimed through customer service, so its availability and any expiry are unverified.
confidence_note: Trial grant is quoted from the vendor's blog post of 2025-10-20 and the register page description; prices from the pricing pages read 2026-11-04. Whether the trial is still granted today, and its duration, were not read (behind a sign-up and customer service).

evidence.proved: The trial is 500 MB, granted after registration through customer service.

extras.rung_note: A rotating residential pool presents a different single address per session (rung 2); the static ISP product would reach rung 5 only if its addresses are registered to an access network, which no page read shows and no address was sampled.

extras.native_vs_broadcast: two kinds of static ISP address at different prices; the registration class of each is unverified
